shared_elements: upright stone slab bearing low-relief carving
division of the surface into horizontal registers or bands
band of repeated geometric pattern (zigzag/net-like) running across the stone
animal or creature forms shown in profile
justification: Both are tall stone monoliths worked in shallow relief and both organise their imagery into stacked horizontal registers, with a repeated geometric band and profile creatures appearing in each. The difference is decisive: A is a dense, uniform grid of small, tightly packed square units of near-equal size and high internal detail, while B carries a few large, widely spaced, smoothly modelled animal figures on open ground, so the scale, density and manner of cutting are entirely unalike.
